who: GPT-6 Astra Pro, main distributed compile review lane
what: Source protocol diagnostic run 46070408800 failed a_late_subscriber_waits_for_the_one_leads_full_tail with 'late subscriber ran a second tail'. Source inspection found that a publication miss can be delayed across another execution's mirror, delivery and removal from Jobs::running, after which Submit creates a fresh execution without another publication check.
cost: A requester can acquire authority to repeat a full compiler tail whose immutable result is already published. The diagnostic does not retain execution IDs, so its exact binding is inferred; a forced-order causal regression is required.
cause: The publication lookup precedes admission, while live coalescing ends when the previous execution completes. Neither side closes the interval between the cache miss and the new binding.
whys: A late requester was allowed to run a second tail.
A cache miss can remain in flight until the previous execution has delivered its immutable publication and left the live index.
Submit coalesces only live executions, and the agent proceeds from its new binding using the earlier miss.
The publication oracle starts with one Execution and cannot exercise cache lookup across two admissions; the socket test did not gate the reader's own admission.
The cache and scheduler have distinct authority, but the client lacked an admission invariant spanning both.
class: stale absence observations authorize work after publication and live-execution retirement
prevention: The independent rule-66 architecture review required a keyed resolving flight, attempt-fenced cache resolution before compiler admission, and retained accepted output independent of subscriber lifetime. Actual Jobs and framed-carrier simulations cover stale completions, cancellation, capacity, delivery loss and restart with planted faults. A forced-order native control delays an initial 404 until the old execution has published and retired.
fix: Implemented the approved resolve-or-join and bounded accepted-result lifetime design, replacing the proposed standalone second lookup. Local carrier v6 returns accepted results directly without resurrecting old subscriptions. Compiler entry requires resolved authority; committed-result knowledge remains terminal across later errors, and imports, uploads and mirror share the request deadline. CommitPublication is explicitly epoch-local acceptance; cross-epoch reuse begins at durable catalog publication.
state: The resolving-flight and retained-result rules are implemented and have actual-core, framed-carrier and adapter simulations with planted controls. Landing requires the shared control inventory, the paired old/new stale-miss regression, normal source CI and exact-tree smoke receipts. This correctness change does not clear the performance candidate's original source protocol failure or establish a latency improvement.
